name: KIVI asymmetric 2-bit KV (2-bit keys / 4-bit values) on Llama-2-class GQA models: ~8x KV compression for a ~2-5% perplexity delta
kv_bytes_per_token_basis: Llama-2-7B MHA: 32 layers x 32 kv heads x 128 head_dim x 2 (K+V) x 0.1875 bytes-equivalent average (2-bit keys + 4-bit values = 3 bits avg / 16) = 262,144 x 3/16 = 49,152 B/token theoretical. 40,960 records the practical per-token resident after KIVI keeps a residual full-precision window (~128 recent tokens) — an approximation, stated as one because the paper reports batch-level compression (peak memory ~2.6x smaller incl. weights, KV alone approaching the ~8x theoretical) rather than a clean per-token figure.
methodology: Research-harness measurement, not a production serving run: KIVI (arXiv:2402.02750), tuning-free asymmetric KV quant — keys per-channel at 2 bits, values per-token at 4 bits, plus a residual window of recent tokens kept full-precision because keys are the sensitive tensor. WikiText-2 perplexity delta on Llama-2/Llama-3 reported ~2-5% at this setting; GSM8K and long-context (LongBench) degradation within noise on most tasks. No TTFT/throughput published in a form this schema can hold — the value of the record is the KV size / quality trade-off, so measured_* are null rather than filled with a derived guess. engine_id vllm records the partial vLLM integration path, not that this number came from vLLM.
notes: The ASYMMETRY is the finding worth keeping: 2-bit keys work because key outliers are per-channel (a per-channel quant groups the outliers together), while values tolerate only ~4 bits per-token — the two tensors are NOT interchangeable and a symmetric 2-bit KV quant fails badly on the same models, which is why kv_cache_dtype gets a dedicated 'kivi' member rather than 'int2'. Real-world engine support is still partial (vLLM partial, llama.cpp none; ktransformers research), so this is closer to research-only deployment than the fp8 record. The quality delta in the research file ('~2-5% ppl delta on Llama-2/3') is the honest range; the paper's own tables are task-dependent and Llama-3-8B reads better than Llama-2-7B.
